Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

somewhere adverb

also someplace, anywhere (after not, if, or in a question), go somewhere, from somewhere, if anywhere

classical

Ter. Ad. 3.4.7: utinam hīc prope adesset alicubi (Lewis & Short)
Atticus in Cic. Att. 9.10: sī salvus sit Pompejus et cōnstiterit alicubi (Lewis & Short)

alicubi

adverb

somewhere (place where)

Some one place, not named; Lewis & Short, after Priscian: alicubi points to some place, usquam to any place at all.

Other words

  • aliquō — somewhere (to some place)

    adverb of motion · also used · classical · Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7: cum aliquō exībimus

    Of going: aliquō exīre, to go off somewhere.

  • alicunde — from somewhere

    adverb of motion from · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.31: praecipitāre alicunde (Lewis & Short)

    Also “from somebody”: alicunde sūmere, to borrow from someone (Ter. Ph. 2.1.70, Lewis & Short).

  • uspiam — somewhere or other, anywhere

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 37: aut uspiam ceciderit; Cic. Att. 16.13b.1: malō esse in Tusculānō aut uspiam in suburbānō (Lewis & Short)

    Rare but classical; mostly in statements (Lewis & Short).

  • usquam — anywhere (after a negative, in questions and conditions)

    adverb · also used · classical · Liv. 21.22.6: neque usquam ā sē dēflecteret oculōs; Cic. Flac. 50: cui nūllus esset usquam cōnsistendī locus (Lewis & Short)

    The “anywhere” of negative sentences, as quisquam is the “anyone” (see someone); “nowhere” is nusquam (Lewis & Short).

  • sīcubi — if anywhere, wherever

    conjunction · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 15.29.1: sīcubi inciderit (Lewis & Short); Liv. 9.41: sīcubi est certāmen (Lewis & Short)

    “If … anywhere” in one word, as sī quis is “if anyone”.

Examples

  • utinam hīc prope adesset alicubi

    if only he were somewhere near hereTer. Ad. 3.4.7 (Lewis & Short)

  • quod ad Pompōniam, sī tibi vidētur, scrībās velim, cum aliquō exībimus eat nōbīscum puerumque ēdūcat.

    as for Pomponia, please write to her, if you agree, that when we go off somewhere she should come with us and bring the boy.Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7

  • nē aut ille alserit, aut uspiam ceciderit, aut perfrēgerit aliquid

    in case he has caught cold, or fallen somewhere, or broken somethingTer. Ad. 36–38

  • proinde sequerētur neque usquam ā sē dēflecteret oculōs

    so he was to follow, and not turn his eyes from him anywhereLiv. 21.22.6

See also anywhere, everywhere, else, where, someone.
